speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash, low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; could you tell me when these symptoms first started and how the rash appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola).

Based on the timeline of fever and prodromal symptoms followed by a maculopapular rash starting on the face and spreading to the trunk and extremities, sparing the perioral area, this is highly characteristic of measles. I am requesting a complete blood count and measles IgM serology to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Measles_IgM
